title: The caret on a caption's empty new line is drawn short
goal: Press Return in an arrow caption and the blinking caret on the fresh line is noticeably shorter than the one on a line with words on it. Nothing moves and nothing is lost, it just looks wrong for the moment before you type.
notes:
CAUSE (the guess in the original note was wrong, kept here so nobody re-runs it): the extra line fragment was NOT losing the caption font. Measured in the probe, the fragment is 16.0 view points, the same as the line above it, and both the typing attributes and the newline character carry .SFNS-Regular at 13.43, which is the 20pt caption face at the walk's 0.6715 zoom. The CARET rect was the thing being cut: AppKit clips an insertion point at the text view's bottom edge, and the caption field's frame is the BUBBLE, which follows the committed text, which trims a trailing Return. So the line the caret waits on hangs below the field and only the part inside it was drawn (9.741 of 16 view points, 14.5 of 23.8 document points).

FIX: Sources/Photonz/CanvasTextEditing.swift layoutCaptionEditor now sizes the FIELD to the laid-out draft (draftHeight: usedRect or the extra line fragment, plus the pill's padding) while the pill view and the published captionDraftPillRect keep following the committed text. The field paints nothing of its own in a caption session so the extra height is invisible. playtestCaptionGeometry reports the pill rect as `bubble` now, not the editor frame, and carries `lineHeight`. Guarded by a new expectCaption claim, "caretHeight": "full" | "short".
acceptance: The caret on an empty new line in a caption is the same height as the caret on a line with words on it
Typing the first character of that line does not change the caret height
The bubble still does not resize on a bare Return

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The note on the task said the extra line fragment was being laid out with typing attributes that had lost the caption font, and that is NOT what is happening: I built a standalone AppKit harness that reproduces draftFont (descriptor plus a scale AffineTransform), the editor's whole configuration and the Return, and the line fragment came out the right height every time, at zoom 1, 0.771 and 0.61. So I put a temporary read-only probe in the caption field and ran the walk. The layout was right all along: extra line fragment 16.0 view points, the same as line 0; the typing font and the font on the newline character are both .SFNS-Regular at 13.43, which is the caption's 20pt face at the walk's 0.6715 zoom. What was wrong was the CARET rect: rawCaret came back (26.1, 21.0, 0.0, 9.741) against a field only 30.741 tall, i.e. cut off exactly at the field's bottom edge. The field is only as tall as the BUBBLE, the bubble follows the committed text, and the commit trims a trailing Return, so the line the caret waits on hangs below the field and AppKit draws the part that fits. 9.741 view points is 14.5 document points, which is the number in the report.

Shortest fix that keeps the rule the last task established: the FIELD is as tall as the draft is laid out (usedRect, or the extra line fragment when the draft ends in a Return, plus the pill's padding), while the BUBBLE keeps following the committed text. The field paints nothing of its own in a caption session (drawsBackground false, no border, the pill view behind it carries the fill), so the extra height is invisible. No second measurer: CaptionMetrics still sizes the pill and this only asks the layout manager how much room the text it has already laid out needs.

Acceptance, each checked against numbers rather than assumed. (1) Empty new line caret: was 'tall 14.5', now 'tall 23.8 of a 23.8 line', the same as every line with words on it, at both the second and the third line. (2) Typing the first character does not change it: 23.8 before the X and 23.8 after. (3) The bubble still does not resize on a bare Return: (620,277,81,46) either side of the Return, and (399,265,301,70) either side of the second one. The probe now reports the bubble as the published pill rect rather than the editor frame, because the field is allowed to be taller than the bubble and the outline check reads that same rectangle.

A walk can now claim it: expectCaption takes caretHeight 'full' or 'short', parsed in PhotonzCore with tests written first, checked in the harness against a line of the caption's face that the field reports. Proved it bites by putting the old one-line field back and rebuilding: step 17 fails with 'the caret is drawn 14.5 points tall where a line of this caption is 23.8: it is being cut off, most likely by a field that is not as tall as the line the caret waits on'. Scripts/test.sh green, 7499 tests. Walks: caption 12/12, text 17/17, select 10/10, outline 4/6 (the two failures are highlight-one-outline-walk and one-outline-two-kinds-walk, both the known empty panel-menu names, folded into walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep).

left rough, not filed: on an empty new line about the bottom half of the caret now hangs below the bubble's edge, because the bubble is deliberately not allowed to grow for a Return with nothing on it. That is the trade the acceptance asks for and it cannot be photographed (the probe window is never the active app, so macOS never blinks an insertion point in it), so rather than file a task on my own judgement it is the second question in the audit for the user to react to. Also left rough: the taller field extends the invisible click target a few points below the pill while a trailing Return is pending, so a click there moves the caret instead of committing.
